meta.name: kitchen-display-queue-builder
meta.objective: Build the Kitchen Display Queue take-home (Express API + React web) task by task, meeting every mandatory PDF requirement inside the time box, with ranking and status rules isolated, marked and tested.

role.persona: Staff full-stack engineer pairing with the author of a take-home. You build small, layered, explainable code in the PDF's vocabulary, test business rules before implementing them, and stop at every gate so the author can review, commit and explain each file.
operating_principles: The PDF is the only source of requirements and this file is its executable plan; never add features, fields, endpoints or dependencies
Treat the PDF as requirements authority; trace work through REQ IDs and section numbers.
Business rules live in the Module as pure functions and declarative tables; Endpoint, Repository and Web hold none
Test first in the Module; every task ends runnable, with its acceptance checks and tests passing
Prefer the smallest code the author can explain in one sentence per file and per function
Stop after each task, report and wait for the author; never write AI chat logs or the AI section of DECISIONS.md
If neither the PDF nor this file answers something that changes behavior, ask; do not guess

context.domain_summary: A restaurant kitchen receives dine_in, takeout and delivery orders. The expeditor uses one screen to see every active order (received or preparing) ranked by a priority score computed at request time, and to move each order through received -> preparing -> ready -> picked_up, or cancel a received order. No authentication, payments or real customer data.
grading_focus: Project organization and clear Endpoint/Module/Repository/Schema boundaries: four API layers named as in §9.1 plus one web app (§1)
Business rules live in Module rather than HTTP, SQL, or the frontend.
Business rules in the right layer: score, sort and state machine only in the Module (§1, §9.1)
Ranking and status rules are isolated, marked, tested, and fast to change in the panel: one rules file plus its matching test (§1, §13)
The author can explain every file and function, including AI-written code (§2)
A smaller result with an honest DECISIONS.md beats a wide one the author cannot explain (§1)

requirements.statement: MenuItem: name unique and non-empty; category in starter | main_course | dessert | drink; prep_time_minutes integer > 0; provided by the seed, no CRUD
Order: customer_name non-empty string; type in dine_in | takeout | delivery; is_vip boolean
Order: placed_at timestamp set on creation; promised_at timestamp or null
Order.status is one of received | preparing | ready | picked_up | cancelled
OrderItem (join table): order_id references an existing Order; menu_item_id references an existing MenuItem; quantity integer > 0
The default queue lists only received and preparing orders; ready, picked_up and cancelled stay out
The queue is sorted by priority score, highest first; the score is computed at request time using the real clock in the running app
All time comparisons use UTC
Type points: dine_in 30, takeout 20, delivery 10
VIP points: +20 if is_vip is true
Wait-time points = min(40, floor(minutes_waiting / 10) * 5); minutes_waiting = whole minutes since placed_at, floored (9 min 50 s = 9 = 0 points)
Promised-time points: promised_at within 30 minutes from now = 25; within 31-60 minutes = 15; more than 60 minutes away or null = 0
Complexity points = min(20, floor(total_prep_minutes / 15) * 5); total_prep_minutes = sum of prep_time_minutes * quantity over all items
Tie-break on equal score: earlier promised_at first (null last), then earlier placed_at, then smaller id
Worked examples with now = 2026-06-15T12:00:00Z: example A scores 60, example B scores 60, and B ranks above A
Only four transitions are legal: received -> preparing, received -> cancelled, preparing -> ready, ready -> picked_up; anything else is rejected
picked_up and cancelled are terminal; no order can skip a step; repeating the same transition is an error, not a silent success
The state machine is enforced on the server: a direct API call with an illegal transition is rejected with a clear error
GET /orders/queue returns received and preparing orders sorted by score; each order includes its computed score
GET /orders/queue accepts the optional query param status=received or status=preparing to filter
POST /orders/:id/start transitions received -> preparing
POST /orders/:id/ready transitions preparing -> ready
POST /orders/:id/pickup transitions ready -> picked_up
POST /orders/:id/cancel transitions received -> cancelled
Illegal transitions and validation errors return a 4xx response with a stable machine-readable error code; the codes are documented in the README
One page, the Kitchen Display: a table of the active queue showing score, customer name, order type, items summary, wait time, promised time, VIP badge and status
The page offers a way to filter by received, preparing or the default active queue
Each order has actions to advance it to its next status; only the action valid for the current status is shown
The page offers a way to cancel a received order
The page shows an empty state when the queue has no orders
When the API rejects a transition, the error is visible on the screen, not only in the browser console
The UI uses MUI with a dense internal-tool layout (ops dashboard), not a marketing page
Score and sort order come from the API; the UI holds no copy of the scoring formula and shows rows in the order the API returns them
One repository with two apps (API and web); no dependency on any private or external repository
API stack: Node.js 22, JavaScript, Express, Sequelize 6, PostgreSQL 16, Jest
The schema is created by Sequelize migrations; sync() is not used for schema creation
The API is organized in layers: Endpoint (thin HTTP), Module (business logic), Repository (data access), Schema (models and migrations)
The priority function is pure: it receives the order data and now, returns a number, and its Jest tests run without PostgreSQL and without mocking Sequelize
Web stack: Vite, React 19, TypeScript, MUI 7
docker-compose.yml starts PostgreSQL 16 only, on host port 5433, with user, password and database all set to kitchen_queue
From a clean machine: docker compose up -d, one install command, one db:setup command (migrations + seed), one dev command (both apps); API on 4000, web on 5173
The seed contains menu items and orders with order items; every seed date is relative to the UTC time when the seed runs, with no hard-coded calendar dates
The seed shows: every order type; a VIP and a non-VIP; a wait-time cap; a complexity cap; a score tie broken by promised_at; received, preparing and at least one ready order
Tests do not use the seed; they pass their own fixtures and a frozen now
Jest priority tests prove: score calculation, both caps, all promised_at buckets (within 30, within 60, beyond, null), tie-break, and a lower base-weight type winning on the rest of the formula
Jest transition tests prove: every legal transition succeeds; skip, repeat and from-terminal transitions are rejected; cancelled and picked-up orders are not in the default queue
Priority tests freeze now; no test calls Date.now() and hopes the clock still matches
README.md has the prerequisites (Docker, Node 22), the four commands to get running, the ports and the API error codes
DECISIONS.md has the sections Scope, Layers, Priority, Transitions, AI and Next, a few short paragraphs each, answering the prompts of §12.1
The AI section of DECISIONS.md names one AI suggestion kept and one rejected or rewritten, quoting the idea and not the tool brand (written by the author)
A root folder ai-logs/ holds the full exported AI conversation history, wrong turns included (exported by the author)
DECISIONS.md notes which extra-point items were attempted and which were left out
The submission is a git repository that can be cloned, containing the API, the web app, migrations, seed and tests
Any deviation from the suggested layout (api/src, web/src, ai-logs/, root files) is explained in DECISIONS.md
The project is designed so that a change to ranking or to status rules is local and quick
With Docker running, both apps boot in a couple of minutes for the panel
POST /orders (API only): items non-empty, each menu_item_id references an existing menu item, each quantity a positive integer; at least one Jest test for a validation error
Vitest component test: the cancel button is shown only for received orders, or the queue table renders an empty state when there are no orders
Playwright happy path: the queue renders a seeded order, the expeditor starts preparation, the status changes on screen; webServer config lets npm run test:e2e boot what it needs
Every queue item carries allowed_actions derived from the transition table; the web renders only those buttons
Every queue item carries minutes_waiting computed by the API with the same now as the score
One error middleware maps domain errors to stable codes with the single body { error: { code, message } }; :id and ?status are validated
The queue is loaded in one eager-loaded query (orders + items + menu items), no N+1; orders.status is indexed
Database constraints mirror §4: foreign keys, unique menu item name, CHECK (quantity > 0), CHECK (prep_time_minutes > 0), NOT NULL
Transitions are race-safe: load (404), transition() (409), then UPDATE ... WHERE id AND status = from; 0 rows affected is 409
Change points carry the markers @rule-change RANKING and @rule-change STATUS in rules files and their tests; README has a 'Where to change the rules' table
Every code file has a header of at most 4 lines and every exported function has JSDoc (api) or TSDoc (web) with @see PDF section
After a successful action the UI refetches the queue with the current filter and changes nothing locally; the action button is disabled while its request is in flight
Setup: npm workspaces + concurrently, .nvmrc and engines on Node 22, .env.example matching docker-compose, @mui/material@^7 and sequelize@^6 pinned, Vite proxy to the API
ai-logs/README.md tells the author what to export and how to name it; the executor never writes logs and reminds the author to export after each task
Machine prerequisites (Node.js 22 active, Docker running with the `docker compose` plugin, git) are checked before T01; if one is missing or wrong the executor stops and the author fixes it

fields.name: name
fields.rules: NOT NULL, UNIQUE; model validate notEmpty

fields.name: category
fields.rules: NOT NULL; model validate isIn starter, main_course, dessert, drink

entities.name: Order

fields.name: id
fields.rules: Primary key, auto-increment; last key of the §5.2 tie-break

fields.name: type
fields.rules: NOT NULL; VARCHAR; model validate isIn ORDER_TYPES (keys of PRIORITY_RULES.typeWeights)

fields.name: placed_at
fields.rules: NOT NULL; defaults to now() so it is set on creation

fields.name: status
fields.rules: NOT NULL; VARCHAR; default 'received'; indexed; model validate isIn ORDER_STATUSES (keys of TRANSITIONS)

relations: All models: underscored true, timestamps false (no columns beyond §4 plus id)

fields.name: order_id
fields.rules: NOT NULL; FK -> orders.id, ON DELETE CASCADE

fields.name: menu_item_id
fields.rules: NOT NULL; FK -> menu_items.id, ON DELETE RESTRICT

priority.pure_function_signature: computePriority(order, now) -> number; order = { type, is_vip, placed_at: Date, promised_at: Date | null, items: [{ prep_time_minutes, quantity }] }; now = Date

components.name: promised
components.formula: ms until promised_at <= 30 min -> 25; > 30 min and <= 60 min -> 15; otherwise or null -> 0

edge_cases: 9 min 50 s waiting is 9 whole minutes = 0 wait points; 10 min 00 s = 5 (§5.1)
An overdue promised_at (negative difference) counts as within 30 min: 25 pts (D-01)
promised_at exactly +30 min = 25; +30 min 30 s = 15; exactly +60 min = 15; +60 min 1 s = 0 (D-02)
promised_at is scored for every order type, dine_in included (D-03)
14 total prep minutes = 0 complexity points; 15 = 5; 60 or more = 20 (cap)
Compare instants with getTime() (UTC ms); never parse or format local time in the Module

state_machine.on_illegal: transition() throws DomainError INVALID_TRANSITION; the error middleware answers 409 { error: { code, message } } and the order stays unchanged

success.body_shape: JSON array of queue items (context.queue_item_dto), already sorted by compareQueue; [] when nothing matches

errors.when: status is present and is not received or preparing (ready, cancelled, empty or unknown values)

success.body_shape: { id, status } of the updated order (status = preparing); the UI refetches the queue

errors.when: Current status is not received (skip, repeat or terminal), or it changed during the request

success.body_shape: { id, status } of the updated order (status = ready); the UI refetches the queue

errors.when: Current status is not preparing (skip, repeat or terminal), or it changed during the request

success.body_shape: { id, status } of the updated order (status = picked_up)

errors.when: Current status is not ready (skip, repeat or terminal), or it changed during the request

success.body_shape: { id, status } of the updated order (status = cancelled); the UI refetches the queue

errors.when: Current status is not received (repeat or terminal), or it changed during the request

params.body: { customer_name, type, is_vip?, promised_at?, items: [{ menu_item_id, quantity }] } (extra T13 only)

success.body_shape: { id, status: 'received', placed_at } of the created order

errors.when: items empty or missing, unknown menu_item_id, quantity not a positive integer, or an invalid order field

fields.name: minutes_waiting
fields.type: integer (whole minutes, same now as score)

ux_ui_rules.rule: One page with one MUI table; columns in order: Score, Customer, Type, Items, Wait, Promised, VIP, Status, Actions
Filter is an exclusive ToggleButtonGroup: Active (no query param, default), Received (?status=received), Preparing (?status=preparing)
Actions cell renders one button per entry of allowed_actions and nothing else; the web never maps status to actions
Cancel is the button for the cancel action; it appears only where allowed_actions includes cancel (received orders today)
When the API returns [], the table body shows one full-width row with the text 'No orders in the queue'
A rejected action shows a dismissible MUI Alert (severity error) above the table with error.code and error.message
Dense ops layout: Table size='small', compact header with title and filter, VIP and status as small Chips, no hero or marketing blocks
Rows are rendered in the order of the API array; no .sort(), no score arithmetic anywhere in web/src
After a successful action, refetch the queue with the current filter; never edit score, order or status locally
The clicked row's action buttons are disabled while its request is in flight, so a double click cannot repeat a transition
Formatting only: items as '2x Grilled Salmon, 1x Caesar Salad'; wait as '{minutes_waiting} min'; promised_at as local HH:mm or a dash

quality_attributes.requirement: Every file states its layer and limits; every exported function states its purpose and PDF section

layers.name: Endpoint
layers.responsibility: HTTP only: read params and query, call one Module function, write the JSON response; map DomainError codes to HTTP statuses
must_not: Call Sequelize, models or repository functions directly
Compute scores, sort, or decide whether a transition is legal

layers.name: Module
layers.responsibility: Business rules: PRIORITY_RULES, computePriority, compareQueue, TRANSITIONS, transition, queue assembly and input validation
must_not: Import Express, Sequelize, models or the repository file (dependencies arrive as an argument)
Read the clock directly; now comes from the injected clock

layers.name: Repository
layers.responsibility: Data access: Sequelize queries, includes and filters; returns plain objects, never model instances
must_not: Score, sort by priority or know which statuses are active (statuses arrive as an argument)

layers.name: Schema
layers.responsibility: Sequelize models, migrations and the seed; database constraints mirroring §4
must_not: Hold literal status or type lists (import ORDER_STATUSES and ORDER_TYPES from the Module)

layers.name: Web
layers.responsibility: One page: fetch the queue, render it in API order, format values, post actions and refetch
must_not: Compute a score or sort rows
Map status to actions (render allowed_actions only)
Change queue rows locally after an action

decisions.choice: An overdue promised_at counts as within 30 minutes: 25 pts
decisions.rationale: Time until promised_at is negative, so it is <= 30 min; a late order must not drop in the queue

decisions.choice: Compare the difference in ms: <= 30 min -> 25; > 30 min and <= 60 min -> 15; otherwise 0
decisions.rationale: Closes the 30-31 min gap of §5.1 with no rounding step: +30:00 = 25, +30:30 = 15, +60:00 = 15, +60:01 = 0

decisions.choice: Score promised_at for every order type, as §5.1 is written
decisions.rationale: §5.1 does not condition on type and 'relevant for' in §4.2 is descriptive; the promise rule gets no type branch

decisions.choice: 400 VALIDATION_ERROR (bad :id or ?status, including status=ready); 404 ORDER_NOT_FOUND; 409 INVALID_TRANSITION
decisions.rationale: Three stable codes cover §7; 409 says the request conflicts with the order's current status
npm latest is 5.2.1; rejected async handlers reach the error middleware with no wrapper (checked on expressjs.com)

decisions.choice: VARCHAR validated by ORDER_STATUSES and ORDER_TYPES exported by the Module; no Postgres ENUM
decisions.rationale: Adding an ENUM value needs a migration and §13 asks for a live rule change, so the lists live in one code file

decisions.choice: Follow the PDF literally: pickup is API-only and covered by tests; the gap is noted in DECISIONS.md Next
decisions.rationale: ready orders leave the queue (§5) and the §7 filter accepts only received or preparing, so no row on screen can offer pickup

decisions.choice: Pure Jest test of the orders module with an in-memory fake repository; no Postgres, no Sequelize mocks
decisions.rationale: Fast and simple; the Module passes ACTIVE_QUEUE_STATUSES to the repository, so one constant drives both

decisions.topic: Valid actions come from the API
decisions.choice: Queue items carry allowed_actions and the POST action routes are registered from the same TRANSITIONS table
decisions.rationale: The state machine stays server-only (§6, §8); a new transition gets its route and its button with no endpoint or web edit

decisions.choice: GET /orders/queue returns a bare JSON array; transition endpoints return 200 { id, status } and the UI refetches
decisions.rationale: §7 does not fix the bodies; these are the smallest shapes that serve §8 and keep the queue as the only source of row data

decisions.choice: Load -> transition() -> UPDATE ... WHERE id AND status = from; 0 rows affected -> 409 INVALID_TRANSITION
decisions.rationale: Two expeditors clicking at once cannot both succeed, and 404 is never confused with 409; no lock or transaction needed

decisions.choice: 500 with code INTERNAL_ERROR in the same error body; unknown routes keep Express's default 404
decisions.rationale: A fallback needs one code to keep the body consistent; it is not a §7 4xx code and adds no validation rule

decisions.choice: Order.hasMany(OrderItem) + OrderItem.belongsTo(MenuItem); timestamps false; CommonJS; models registered explicitly
decisions.rationale: The join row carries data (quantity) so it is its own model; no columns beyond §4; sequelize-cli expects CommonJS

decisions.choice: The seeder truncates the three tables (RESTART IDENTITY) before inserting; db:setup = migrate + seed
decisions.rationale: Re-running db:setup before the panel refreshes the relative dates and resets the demo state (§9.5, §13)

decisions.choice: Add docs/ (the PDF) and ai-logs/00-planning/; keep *.test.js next to the module files; root e2e/ only if T15 runs
decisions.rationale: A test beside its rules file makes the change point obvious; planning artifacts double as AI evidence. Explained in DECISIONS.md

decisions.choice: Recommended order kept; one task added (T05 orders module) between transitions and Repository
decisions.rationale: Queue assembly and applyAction are Module logic tested with a fake repository, so they come before the real one

decisions.choice: Module functions take deps = { repository, clock } as first argument; app.js builds deps once
decisions.rationale: Plain argument passing, no DI container: the Module never imports Sequelize and tests pass a fake repository and a fixed clock

decisions.choice: The PDF is docs/RxRedefined Staff Engineer Take-home test.pdf; meta.source_of_truth keeps the planning literal, so locate it with Glob docs/*.pdf
decisions.rationale: The author saved the file under its original name; the planning prompt fixes the literal path and says to Glob when the path differs

decisions.choice: context.doc_facts were checked on the official sites and npm instead of Context7; the executor does not query again
decisions.rationale: Context7 was not connected and the author asked to verify on the current websites; each doc_facts entry names its source
